title: Memory dimension detection in open quantum dynamics via pseudo-control
authors: Chang Liu, Alexander Yosifov, Ximing Wang, Zhenhuan Liu, Jinzhao Sun
abstract: Characterising open quantum dynamics requires identifying the environmental degrees of freedom that shape the system's evolution. The memory dimension, defined as the size of the smallest effective memory needed to reproduce this influence, quantifies the dynamically relevant environmental resources and provides a common basis for comparing different many-body environments. Here we introduce a pseudo-control protocol that encodes information about the memory dimension in an experimentally accessible interference matrix, whose rank certifies a lower bound on this dimension without direct access to the environment or full process-tensor tomography. Applied to quantum many-body environments, the protocol allows flexible adjustment of the interaction and interval times, revealing how these parameters, environmental dynamics, and system-environment interactions shape detectable memory. Our approach provides a new operational technique for characterising open quantum dynamics and probing the structure of system-environment interactions through their memory signatures.
summary: This paper introduces a novel 'pseudo-control protocol' to estimate the memory dimension of open quantum dynamics. By analyzing the rank of an interference matrix derived from two sequential system-environment interactions, the authors establish a lower bound on the environmental memory. This technique allows for the characterization of complex system-environment interactions in many-body quantum systems without requiring full environmental tomography.
main_problem: The paper aims to characterize the memory dimension of open quantum dynamics, which quantifies the essential environmental resources shaping system evolution.
main_result: A pseudo-control protocol was developed that uses the rank of an interference matrix to establish a lower bound on the memory dimension without full process tomography.
method: The protocol involves comparing the system's evolution under two separate interactions separated by a waiting time, generating an interference matrix whose rank is analyzed.
model_or_system: The study focuses on open quantum dynamics involving a system (S) coupled to an environment (E), modeled using Lindblad-type master equations for the evolution during interaction and waiting periods.
key_observables: The primary observable is the 'resolved rank' ($r_\epsilon$) of the interference matrix (MRS), which provides a lower bound on the memory dimension ($d_m \ge \lceil\sqrt{r_\epsilon}ceil$).
important_parameters: Interaction time ($	au$), interval time ($T$), coupling strength ($\lambda$), and the specific coupling geometry (boundary vs. ladder).
main_assumptions:
The bound derived from the rank is one-sided (high rank $\implies$ large memory, but low rank $
ot\implies$ little memory). The analysis relies on a fixed resolution scale ($\epsilon$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the temporal dependence of the resolved rank ($r_\epsilon$) for various environmental models (A-E) under changes in $	au$ and $T$, and compare the spectral evolution between dissipative (Model C) and coherent (Model E) environments.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the memory dimension concept, details the pseudo-control protocol and the resulting rank bound, and then applies this method to test various quantum many-body models (Ising, XXZ) under different environmental coupling geometries and time scales.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, experimentally accessible diagnostic tool for characterizing complex, non-Markovian environmental coupling in quantum systems, which is crucial for understanding decoherence mechanisms in quantum computation and simulation.
